insurer: Aditya Birla Health Insurance Co. Limited
sumInsured: Not specified in provided extract (as per Policy Schedule / Product Benefit Table)

great.name: Restore Benefit
great.quote: “Binge Refill ... provide for a refill of the Sum Insured, unlimited times during the Policy Year ... The Refill of Sum Insured shall be available for all subsequent claims also and to any Illness / Injury (including its complications) for which a claim has been admitted for the Insured Person during that Policy Year.”
great.explanation: Sum Insured gets refilled unlimited times during the policy year and can be used for subsequent claims including the same illness/injury and its complications. This greatly reduces the chance of running out of cover after one large claim.

great.name: NCB
great.quote: “In the event of a claim impacting the eligibility of a No Claim Bonus, the accumulated No Claim Bonus shall be reduced by the percentage of Sum Insured as accumulated in the previous Policy Year...”
great.explanation: On a claim, the accumulated No Claim Bonus is reduced by a percentage instead of being wiped out to zero. This is better than many plans where the entire bonus resets after a claim.

good.name: Initial Waiting Period
good.quote: “30-day waiting period ... Expenses related to the treatment of any illness within 30 days from the first policy commencement date shall be excluded except claims arising due to an accident”
good.explanation: Illness-related treatment is not covered for the first 30 days from the first policy start date, but accidents are covered from day one. This is a standard market waiting period.

good.name: Specific Illness Waiting
good.quote: “Expenses related to the treatment of the listed Conditions, surgeries/treatments shall be excluded until the expiry of 24 months of continuous coverage after the date of inception of the first policy with Us.”
good.explanation: Listed diseases/surgeries are covered only after 24 months of continuous coverage from the first policy inception. This is in line with common industry practice.

good.name: Domiciliary Hospitalization
good.quote: “We shall cover the Medical Expenses incurred for the Insured Person’s Domiciliary Hospitalization, up to the Sum Insured as specified in the Policy Schedule / Product Benefit Table of this Policy”
good.explanation: Home-based treatment that qualifies as domiciliary hospitalization is covered up to the Sum Insured as per the schedule/benefit table. This helps when hospital admission isn’t possible but hospital-level care is needed at home.

good.name: Modern Treatments
good.quote: “We shall cover the Medical Expenses for the following modern treatment procedures ... up to the Sum Insured specified in the Policy Schedule / Product Benefit Table of this Policy.”
good.explanation: Modern treatment procedures are covered up to the Sum Insured as per the schedule/benefit table. This supports access to newer, often expensive procedures, subject to plan limits.

bad.name: Consumables
bad.quote: “Non-Medical expenses ... As mentioned under Annexure (I) List II, III & IV will be excluded unless forms a part of In-patient hospitalization.” AND “Non-Medical Expense waiver ... We shall cover cost of Non-Medical Items ... listed under Annexure I ...”
bad.reference: Section D.23 Non-Medical expenses; Section C.IV (w) Non-Medical Expense waiver
bad.explanation: Non-medical/consumable items listed in Annexure I are excluded by default, and are covered only if the optional Non-Medical Expense waiver is in force. This can create significant out-of-pocket costs during hospitalization if you don’t buy the add-on.

unclear.name: Room Rent
unclear.quote: “Room Rent ... up to the limits as specified in the Policy Schedule / Product Benefit Table of this Policy;”
unclear.explanation: Room rent is payable only up to the limit shown in the Policy Schedule/Product Benefit Table, but the cap is not stated in the wording extract. If the schedule has a rupee/day cap, it can increase your share of the bill and may trigger proportionate deductions.

unclear.name: Pre-hospitalization Cover
unclear.quote: “We shall cover ... for the number of days in accordance with the limits specified in the Policy Schedule / Product Benefit Table of this Policy”
unclear.explanation: Pre-hospitalization expenses are covered for the number of days shown in the Policy Schedule/Product Benefit Table, but the duration is not stated in the extract. Your reimbursement for tests/consultations before admission depends on that schedule limit.

unclear.name: Post-hospitalization Cover
unclear.quote: “We shall cover ... for the number of days specified in the Policy Schedule / Product Benefit Table of this Policy”
unclear.explanation: Post-hospitalization expenses are covered for the number of days shown in the Policy Schedule/Product Benefit Table, but the duration is not stated in the extract. Follow-up medicine and consultation coverage after discharge will depend on that limit.

unclear.name: PED Waiting Period
unclear.quote: “Expenses related to the treatment of a pre-existing Disease (PED) ... shall be excluded until the expiry of months as specified in the Policy Schedule / Product Benefit Table of this Policy...”
unclear.explanation: Pre-existing diseases are not covered until the waiting period (in months) mentioned in the Policy Schedule/Product Benefit Table is completed. The exact duration isn’t visible in the extract, so you must check the schedule to know when PED cover starts.

disclaimer: Standard IRDAI exclusions apply. Please verify all details with your insurer or policy document.
